knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A leaning load over a softened floor is a combined sign of possible collapse.
Testing a load by pushing can cause the collapse the lesson is meant to prevent.
Alteration of an unstable load needs a competent assessment, recorded first.

practicalCriteria: In a photographed or drawn scene, the learner names at least three instability signs and draws the boundary without entering it.
The learner writes the referral note with the time, the signs and the requested assessor.
passRule: Knowledge checks only: three of three correct is a reading pass. It is not practical competence. Practical sign-off: an assessor observes each practical criterion and records it as met or not met.
evidenceRequired: Knowledge-check result recorded by the assessor
Completed training worksheet or role-play record for the scenario, marked by a trainer
stopWorkCriteria: A load is pushed, climbed on or altered before a competent assessment.
People remain under a leaning load.
